title: Move away from the wire
hook: Change perpendicular distance and predict magnetic-field magnitude.
misconception: magnetic-field magnitude doubles when perpendicular distance doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply B = μ₀I/(2πr) to compare magnetic-field magnitude when perpendicular distance changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal long straight wire in vacuum carrying fixed current, B = μ₀I/(2πr). When perpendicular distance doubles, magnetic-field magnitude becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model B = μ₀I/(2πr); scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal long straight wire in vacuum carrying fixed current, with a nonzero initial result. If perpendicular distance triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on magnetic-field magnitude?
recall.why: Apply B = μ₀I/(2πr) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
